title: Eleven Years of Luck
subtitle: 奖金与报酬 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 奖金与报酬（社会服务与人际沟通·职业与工作）
meta: 主题语境：奖金与报酬（社会服务与人际沟通·职业与工作）　|　核心词汇：bonus　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 bonus 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1961 my mother was sent to count ① a bonus she could not spend, and she said the spending was the whole of the lesson. The ② bonus, meaning the money and not the praise, was fifty pounds and was shared by whoever came last; a bonus, she said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ bonus in that ledger had the same date, and the ④ bonus at the end, meaning the one the manager signed and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever counted properly. A bonus, my grandmother said, is nine parts luck and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the luck is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ bonus was the whole of the year, meaning the luck it stood for and not the money. The ⑥ bonus, meaning the luck and not any of that, is the only thing in a year that everybody expects and nobody questions; a bonus, he said, is either something you count or the only word that means both money and luck. She said the year is the part they remember.

By 1973 the ⑦ bonus had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the luck. The ⑧ bonus of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was fifty pounds and eleven years of counting; a bonus, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ bonus I remember is the one at the end, which was paid in 1978 and is still described as the best in the county. A ⑩ bonus, my grandmother said in 1984, is the only thing that improves by being shared; every bonus, she said, is a year that has agreed to look like money. She said the year was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 奖金（指那笔钱本身，与表扬相对）
C. 固定搭配：count a bonus 清点一笔奖金
D. n. 奖金（指账簿上每一笔）
E. n. 奖金（指末尾那一笔）
F. n. 额外的好处（抽象：与钱相对）
G. n. 那份运气（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a bonus she could not spend
The bonus, meaning the money and not the praise
bonus was the whole of the year
the bonus had become a number in a report
The bonus of the whole thing
A bonus, my grandmother said in 1984

answers.why: count a bonus 意为“清点一笔奖金”，1961 年母亲被派去清点一笔她花不出去的奖金。
bonus 意为“奖金”，指那笔钱本身而不是表扬，共五十英镑，由最后走的人分掉。
bonus 指账簿上每一笔奖金，每一笔都是同一个日期。
bonus 指末尾那一笔（经理签的那一笔），是唯一有人认真清点过的。
bonus 意为“额外的好处”，与钱相对，父亲说 bonus 就是那一年的全部。
bonus 为抽象用法，指那份运气本身，是一年里人人都期待、却没人质疑的东西。
bonus 意为“奖金、红利”，到 1973 年这笔 bonus 成了报告里的一个数字。
bonus 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是五十英镑和十一年的清点。
bonus 意为“奖金”，我记得的是末尾那一笔，1978 年发放，至今仍被说成全县最好的。
bonus 为抽象总称，祖母说奖金是唯一会因为被分掉而变好的东西。
